action: Apply Check Point's fixes for CVE-2026-123039 and CVE-2026-107484 on firewalls, management and log servers, Multi-Domain servers and Maestro Orchestrator. Read the Check Point advisories and the CISA catalog entry linked from the advisory.
exec: Canada's national agency confirms active exploitation of a Check Point flaw; firewalls and their management servers need the vendor fix now.
plain: Canada's cyber agency warned that a flaw in Check Point firewall software is being used by attackers to take full control of devices they have already reached, and told organisations to install Check Point's fixes.
products: Check Point Management and Log Servers

key_findings: Affected, in multiple versions: Check Point Force Firewalls, Management and Log Servers, Multi-Domain Security Management and Log Server, and Maestro Orchestrator.
CVE-2026-123039 is a local privilege escalation to root in the DynamicCLI process through a world-writable control socket.
CVE-2026-107484 is an input validation flaw in Gaia Portal backend handlers that lets an authenticated user escalate privileges.
The advisory relays Check Point's statement that CVE-2026-123039 is being exploited in the wild.
Update 1 of November 13 notes that CISA added CVE-2026-123039 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog.
recommendations: Review the Check Point advisories linked from the advisory.
Review the CISA Known Exploited Vulnerabilities entry for CVE-2026-123039.
Apply the necessary updates as they become available.

summary: Cyber Centre advisory AV26-1154, issued November 12 and updated the next day, covers two flaws across multiple versions of Check Point Force firewalls, management and log servers, Multi-Domain products and Maestro Orchestrator. It relays Check Point's statement that CVE-2026-123039, a local escalation to root, is being exploited in the wild. Update 1 records that CISA added that flaw to its exploited-vulnerabilities catalog on November 13.
title: Canadian Centre for Cyber Security: Check Point advisory AV26-1154 updated as Gaia flaw is exploited

validation.note: Reviewed against the original Canadian Centre for Cyber Security document.
